issue.title: iPad: clearing a crayon drawing freezes the app and gets it killed for memory
issue.body:
Part of #2978 (crash hunt). Release-blocking: it is the crash the owner reported, reproduced on the physical iPad.

## Signature

iOS jetsam memory kill, with no crash report written:

```
launchd: exited with exit reason (namespace: 1 code: 0x7) - JETSAM_REASON_MEMORY_PERPROCESSLIMIT
SpringBoard: Process exited: <RBSProcessExitStatus| domain:jetsam(1) code:per-process-limit(7)>
```

Seconds before the kill, the system reclaims other long-idle apps (`JETSAM_REASON_MEMORY_LONGIDLE_EXIT`), and the screen stays frozen while it happens. That matches the owner's report: "at first, screen froze and stayed there for ~5s and then app completely shut down and went to home screen".

## Repro

On a 12.9-inch iPad, Release build at 645ffd4c2fffa39b25bb04f077d514f457b2cece:

1. Choose **Crayon**.
2. Draw several strokes. 6 strokes are enough to see the spike; 24 reach the cap.
3. Drag Clear past the ring and let go.

Footprint (DVT sysmon, `physFootprint`) at the commit:

| Cleared crayon strokes | Before | Peak | After |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 6 | 290 MB | 1,405 MB | 689 MB |
| 6 | 460 MB | 1,254 MB | 674 MB |
| 24 | 353 MB | 4,628 MB | 323 MB (the next touch interrupted it) |
| 24 | | | killed: `per-process-limit` |

Controls: the same sequence with **Pen** peaks at 279 MB. Crayon strokes without a Clear peak at 263 MB.

## Cause

The departing page that flies into the Clear button (`RsdClearUnderlay`'s `DepartingSheet`) draws the cleared drawing again through react-native-svg (`InkScene`). Each crayon pass is wrapped in `CrayonGlaze`, an SVG `<Filter>` (FeBlend with `BackgroundImage`, then FeComposite) whose filter region is the whole paper. The Time Profiler stack during the spike, on the main thread inside a Core Animation commit:

```
-[RNSVGSvgView drawRect:]
  -[RNSVGRenderable renderTo:rect:] > -[RNSVGFilter applyFilter:backgroundImg:renderableBounds:canvasBounds:ctm:]
    CI::MetalTextureManager::texture_for_CGImage > -[AGXG13GFamilyTexture replaceRegion:...]
    CI::image_render_to_bitmap > CIMetalTextureGetBytes
  CGDisplayListDrawInContextDelegate > ripc_DrawImage > RGBAf16_image (8 bytes per pixel)
```

Every filtered group copies the full canvas through Core Image at half-float precision, so memory grows with the number of crayon passes times the paper's pixels. The main thread is held throughout, which is the freeze. Diagnostic logging confirmed `InkScene` renders the departing drawing (6 strokes, all crayon) three times at the commit instant. Native captures already avoid this path: `PictureCapture` uses the Skia layer's raster (`readyPlan`'s `ink`), so the departing sheet is the only native consumer of the crayon SVG scene.

Shipping flies a bitmap of the canvas (`web/src/lib/drawing/inkMotion.ts` `clear()`), never a vector re-render, which is why shipping never crashed here.

## Fix direction

On native, fly a snapshot of the live Skia ink layer (the pixels already on screen) in the departing sheet instead of re-rendering the SVG scene. RN web keeps its SVG ink.
issue.display_title: iPad: clearing a crayon drawing freezes the app and gets it killed for memory

comments.body:
The scenario reran to the bar on the physical iPad, so this closes.

- **Build.** The fix is #3036, merged as f27c58f3aa7796c8463ab25893ef72ec626c93e6. The iPad ran its PR head, 4cbd0b7130933d89ca30c4828971c21b880c42d6, which has the same tree (5708e7e66d4937b8cdcb6d69402dbfceb4e85e53).
- **The owner's gesture as a script (S1).** 12 Crayon strokes, then Clear dragged back and forth across the accept ring at 6 Hz for 3 s nominal, released past it, then 10 s idle.
  - Alive in 6 of 6 RN runs and 6 of 6 runs of the v1.6.0 reference.
- **The rest of the pre-registered matrix on the iPad is also alive on both arms:**
  - S2, toddler scribble (2 runs each);
  - S4, lifecycle under load (1 run of 2 cycles each);
  - S5, a 300-stroke session (1 each);
  - S6, audio collisions (2 each).
  - One RN S2 run wrote a non-fatal `cpu_resource` report ("Action taken: none"); it is counted as alive.
- **Exit records.** The iPad's unified log was collected after the matrix (from 03:30Z). It holds no `JETSAM_REASON_MEMORY_PERPROCESSLIMIT`, signal or watchdog exit for either app.
- **Memory, for the record.**
  - Before the fix, 6 Crayon strokes peaked at 1,254–1,405 MB, and 24 strokes reached 4,628 MB or were killed.
  - After it, the same runs measured 359 and 396 MB.

The full crash-hunt record, with every target and both arms, is going into `docs/scratchpad/2026-10-18-device-parity/results/`.
